sources.entry: Open Food Network - Online marketplace for local food. It enables a network of independent online food stores that connect farmers and food hubs with individuals and local businesses. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Ruby

summary.one_liner: Open Food Network is an open-source, not-for-profit online marketplace software platform that lets independent online food stores connect farmers and food hubs with individuals and local businesses.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes the Open Food Network as an online marketplace for local food that enables a network of independent online food stores. It connects farmers and food hubs (including co-ops, online farmers markets, and independent food businesses) with individuals and local businesses. The README says it is meant to give farmers and food hubs an easier and fairer way to distribute their food. It is supported by the Open Food Foundation and a network of global affiliates. The README does not detail specific features; it points to a separate User Guide for a feature list and tutorials. Contributor guidance (Slack, Handbook, GETTING_STARTED and CONTRIBUTING guides) and links to Ansible provisioning playbooks (ofn-install) and a Super Admin Guide are also referenced.
use_cases: Running an online farmers market or food hub store
Selling local food directly from farmers to consumers
Distributing produce through co-ops and food hubs
Hosting a multi-vendor online food ordering marketplace
Provisioning a server for a community food network using Ansible playbooks
how_to_run: See the GETTING_STARTED guide in the repository for development environment setup
See the CONTRIBUTING guide for contribution workflow
See the ofn-install project for Ansible provisioning playbooks
See the Super Admin Guide for configuring new servers
notable: Built for a network of independent online food stores rather than a single storefront
Not-for-profit, open-source project supported by the Open Food Foundation and global affiliates
Ansible playbooks available separately via ofn-install for server provisioning
Uses BrowserStack and KnapsackPro for testing, both provided free to open source projects
caveats: README does not list specific features or a setup command; it defers to external guides
Development setup requires following separate GETTING_STARTED documentation
